hero.headline: Pulte Homes Targets St. Lucie County Bargain Hunters with New Development
hero.body:
Pulte Homes is bringing new housing to St. Lucie County, targeting South Florida buyers looking for more affordable options than what's available in more expensive coastal markets. The national homebuilder is focusing on the county as part of its strategy to serve bargain hunters in the region.

St. Lucie County has emerged as an attractive market for developers and buyers alike, offering lower price points than neighboring counties to the south while still providing access to the broader South Florida region. The area has seen steady growth as housing costs in traditional coastal markets have priced out many buyers.

Pulte's decision to expand in St. Lucie County reflects broader trends in the regional housing market, where buyers are increasingly willing to move farther north along the Treasure Coast to find more affordable housing options. The development represents a significant investment in the local economy and housing supply.

The project is expected to bring new residents and economic activity to St. Lucie County. Pulte is one of the nation's largest homebuilders and has been active in Florida markets for years, bringing experience in developing residential communities that serve a range of price points.

cards.headline: Jacksonville Mayor Deegan to Address Property Tax Overhaul Headed to November Ballot
cards.body:

The measure is now headed to the ballot in November, where Florida voters will decide whether to approve the significant changes to the state's property tax system.

The property tax overhaul emerged from a special legislative session and represents one of the most substantial proposed changes to Florida's tax structure in recent years. State lawmakers advanced the measure through both chambers before sending it to voters for final approval. The plan would affect property owners across Florida, though the specific details of the tax changes and their fiscal impact on local governments remain central to the ongoing discussion.

Mayor Deegan's briefing comes as local officials across Florida work to understand how the proposed overhaul would affect municipal budgets and services. Property taxes serve as a critical revenue source for cities, counties, and school districts throughout the state, funding essential services including public safety, infrastructure, and education. Any significant change to the property tax system could require local governments to adjust their budgets and potentially reconsider service levels or seek alternative revenue sources.

The November ballot will give Florida voters the opportunity to weigh in directly on the tax overhaul. Between now and the election, local officials, advocacy groups, and political organizations are expected to mount campaigns both supporting and opposing the measure. Jacksonville represents one of Florida's largest cities, and the mayor's perspective on the proposal will likely influence discussions in other major metropolitan areas across the state. The outcome of the November vote will determine whether Florida makes sweeping changes to a property tax system that has been in place for decades and affects millions of homeowners and businesses statewide.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce coral reef protections rolled back despite rally to save rare ecosystem
cards.body:
A federally appointed council voted to roll back longstanding protections for the Oculina Bank, a rare deep-water coral reef located just off the coast of Fort Pierce. Dozens of community members gathered at the Blake Library in Martin County to rally for the reef, which scientists say is found nowhere else on Earth and supports more than 2,000 marine species.

The reef sits hundreds of feet below the surface and thrives in deep, dark waters without the sunlight most corals require. Scientists warn that reopening parts of the reef to shrimp trawling could irreparably damage what little remains after trawling destroyed as much as 90% of the reef before federal protections were put in place decades ago. Dr. Grant Gilmore, a scientist who has dived the reef, said the coral provides critical habitat and food for fish in the ecosystem.

The proposals to reopen the reef followed a Trump executive order issued in April 2025 that directed eight regional councils nationwide to reinvigorate the fishing industry. Bob Zales, executive director of the Southeastern Fishing Association and a generational shrimper, argued that reopening access is essential for the struggling rock shrimp industry. Council data shows the rock shrimp industry has plummeted from over 700 trips per year in the mid-1990s to under 100 since 2010, with just 12 active boats in 2018.

Mark Perry, executive director of the Florida Oceanographic Society, joined Gilmore in urging the public to help save the reef at the gathering. The federal agency is preparing a final ruling on the protections. Scientists emphasized that corals grow very slowly and that worldwide coral populations are already in trouble, making further destruction particularly concerning for this ecosystem found only in waters off Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman sentenced to 3 years in prison for running illegal med spa out of backyard shed
cards.body:
Rosa Mena, 50, has been sentenced to three years in prison and five years of probation after operating an unlicensed medical spa out of a shed behind her home on the 5000 block of Northwest Coosa Drive in Port St. Lucie. Mena ran the business under the name Miracle Hand and Spa, offering Botox injections and other cosmetic procedures without proper medical credentials.

The case came to light in May 2025 when a victim reported experiencing partial facial paralysis after receiving 62 units of Botox injections from Mena. The victim, who had been referred to the business by coworkers, paid $325 for the services. When the victim reported the paralysis, Mena refunded the money but asked her to return for another injection of vitamins to reverse the effects. After the paralysis continued, the victim requested proof of Mena's medical license, and Mena provided an altered phlebotomy certificate that had actually expired in February 2024. Mena also falsely claimed to be a doctor from the Dominican Republic.

A multi-agency investigation involving Port St. Lucie Police, PSL Code Enforcement, the PSL Building Department, PSL Business Tax and the Florida Department of Health led to a search warrant at Mena's residence. Detectives discovered medical beds, fat sculpting machines, laser hair removal equipment, laser liposuction machines and injection devices for fillers and Botox inside the backyard shed.

Mena was charged with three counts of aggravated battery causing bodily harm, three counts of practicing medicine without an active license, one count of fraud-swindle obtain property $300 or more, one count of fraud-swindle obtain property under $20,000 and one count of use of two-way communication device to facilitate a felony. The sentence reflects the serious nature of performing medical procedures without proper licensing or training.

cards.headline: Florida property tax cut proposal could reshape local government funding across Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: A property tax cut proposal passed by Florida lawmakers on Tuesday would increase the homestead exemption from $50,000 to $250,000 over two years, but voters must approve it in November and local experts are divided on the consequences for county services and fees.
cards.body:
Florida lawmakers on Tuesday passed a property tax cut proposal that would increase the homestead exemption from $50,000 to $250,000 over two years, with inflation adjustments beginning in 2029. The bill requires approval from 60% of voters in November. The measure would also lower assessment caps on non-homesteaded properties from 10% to 5%.

Local experts are divided on how the tax cut would affect other costs. Real estate attorney Steve Wallace, based in Boynton Beach, raised the possibility of new fees tied to local services such as the sheriff's office and fire rescue. CPA Paul Miller suggested businesses could end up carrying more of the financial burden to offset lost revenue through annual fees. Municipal attorney Raul Gastesi offered a different perspective, suggesting the measure could push home prices higher because buyers would have more money at their disposal.

All four experts acknowledged there are significant unknowns about how counties, municipalities and markets might respond to decreasing property tax revenue. As with any ballot measure that passes, lawmakers would need to return to Tallahassee to work out the specifics in a bill to implement the changes. The outcome could significantly affect how Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties fund local services and operations.

cards.headline: Activists rally in Martin County to save rare coral reef off Fort Pierce coast
cards.teaser: Community members gathered at Blake Library in Martin County to fight for protections of the Oculina Bank, a unique deep-water coral reef located off Fort Pierce that is found nowhere else on Earth.
cards.body:
Dozens of community members gathered at the Blake Library in Martin County after a federally appointed council voted to roll back longstanding protections for the Oculina Bank, a rare deep-water coral reef found only off the coast of Fort Pierce. The reef sits hundreds of feet below the surface and, unlike most coral that requires shallow sunlight, thrives in deep, dark waters. The reef is home to more than 2,000 marine species.

Dr. Grant Gilmore, a scientist who has dived the rare reef, expressed concern about the ecosystem at the rally. 'Very concerned about an ecosystem point of view, where your fish don't exist in a vacuum, they need a habitat, they need food,' Gilmore said. 'The coral reef was giving them habitat and food. You take that away, you don't have the fish.' Mark Perry, Executive Director of the Florida Oceanographic Society, joined Gilmore in urging the public to help save the reef. Scientists warn that shrimp trawling destroyed as much as 90% of the reef before federal protections were put in place decades ago.

Two proposals would reopen parts of the reef to shrimp trawling following a Trump Executive order issued in April 2025 that tasked regional councils to find ways to reinvigorate fishing industries. Bob Zales, executive director of the Southeastern Fishing Association and a generational shrimper, believes reopening the Oculina Bank is essential for the struggling rock shrimp industry. Council data shows the rock shrimp industry has plummeted from over 700 trips per year in the mid-1990s to under 100 since 2010, with the number of active rock shrimpers dropping from 144 in 1996 to less than 30, with just 12 active boats in 2018.

cards.headline: 12 Make-A-Wish children sworn in as junior deputies at St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office
cards.teaser: Sheriff Richard Del Toro honored 12 children from the Make-A-Wish Foundation, giving them badges and showing them what law enforcement is all about.
cards.body:
Twelve children from the Make-A-Wish Foundation were sworn in as junior deputies by St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro on Wednesday. 'This is one of the greatest days in my career,' Del Toro said during the ceremony at the sheriff's office.

Among the new junior deputies were twins Mia and Daryl Nyack. In 2023, Mia was diagnosed with aplastic anemia, a blood disorder, and needed a bone marrow transplant. Her twin brother Daryl donated his bone marrow to save his sister's life, enduring significant pain and time in a wheelchair. 'I was scared, but then he made me feel safe,' Mia said about her brother. Another junior deputy, Tobias, was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia in 2022. His mother Charity Deleon said, 'We even lost him at one point, and they were able to bring him back, and he miraculously recovered.'

The junior deputies received badges, toured the sheriff's office, and saw demonstrations from the helicopter unit, SWAT team and K-9 units. Deleon thanked the sheriff's office, saying, 'Thank you for making the time and the energy to welcome our children into the community, and to remind them that they're important.' Sheriff Del Toro said the children left an impression on his department as well: 'You made our wish come true.'

When that trust is violated through criminal conduct, it creates alarm among parents throughout the affected school district and prompts reviews of hiring, training, and supervision practices.

The affidavit provides additional information about the allegations, though the case remains under active investigation. St. Lucie County families whose children ride district buses will be watching closely to see what steps school officials take to address safety concerns and prevent future incidents. The district operates hundreds of bus routes daily, serving thousands of students across elementary, middle, and high schools throughout the county.

cards.headline: Split vote closes and merges county middle schools
cards.teaser: A divided vote has resulted in the closure and consolidation of middle schools in a county district, a decision that will reshape where students attend classes.
cards.body:
Middle schools will close and merge following a split vote by a county school board, a contentious decision that will force students into new schools and likely redraw attendance boundaries. The vote reflects deep division among board members about how to address enrollment patterns, facility conditions, or budget pressures affecting middle school operations.

School closures and consolidations rank among the most difficult decisions facing school boards, often triggering strong reactions from parents, teachers, and communities that lose neighborhood schools. Students will face transitions to new buildings, new teachers, and new peer groups, while staff may be reassigned or face job uncertainty.

The split vote suggests the decision was far from unanimous, with at least some board members voting against the consolidation plan. Middle school closures typically involve complex factors including declining enrollment, aging facilities requiring expensive repairs, or district efforts to balance budgets by operating fewer buildings. Families in affected attendance zones will need to adjust to new school assignments in the coming academic year.

cards.headline: Summer vacation dates set for St. Lucie, Martin, and Indian River schools
cards.teaser: School districts across the Treasure Coast have established their summer vacation schedules for 2026.
cards.body:
Families in St. Lucie, Martin, and Indian River counties now know when students will be out of school for summer vacation in 2026. The vacation dates determine when the current school year ends and when students return for the next academic year, critical information for parents planning summer childcare, camps, and family trips.

School calendars vary slightly from district to district based on board decisions, required instructional days, and local preferences about factors like starting before or after Labor Day. St. Lucie County schools serve Port St. Lucie and Fort Pierce, Martin County schools serve Stuart, Jensen Beach, Palm City, and Hobe Sound, while Indian River County schools serve Vero Beach, Sebastian, and Fellsmere.

Summer break represents the longest stretch when students are out of school, typically running from late May or early June through mid-August. The schedules help families coordinate work schedules, plan vacations, and arrange summer activities for children. Teachers and school staff also follow these calendars, with many using the break for professional development, curriculum planning, or personal time before the next school year begins.

cards.headline: State legislature passes property tax exemption expansion, puts constitutional amendment on ballot
cards.teaser: Florida lawmakers have approved expanding the homestead property tax exemption and will ask voters to approve the change through a constitutional amendment.
cards.body:
The Florida legislature has passed a measure to expand the homestead property tax exemption, setting up a constitutional amendment vote that could reduce tax bills for homeowners across the Treasure Coast and throughout the state. The expansion would increase the amount of a home's value that is exempt from property taxes, potentially saving homeowners hundreds of dollars annually.

Homestead exemptions reduce the taxable value of primary residences, lowering what homeowners pay to fund county government, school districts, and other local services. The current exemption shields the first $25,000 of home value from all property taxes and an additional $25,000 from non-school taxes. Any expansion would increase those thresholds, though the specific new amounts depend on the final amendment language.

The measure now goes to voters as a constitutional amendment, requiring approval from 60% of those casting ballots. If passed, the exemption expansion would affect homeowners in Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties, as well as throughout Florida. However, reducing property tax revenue also means less money for local services including schools, roads, public safety, and other programs funded through property taxes unless replaced by other revenue sources or offset by budget cuts.

The honors celebrate the region's top talent at the conclusion of another competitive high school baseball campaign.

All-Area teams recognize the best players across multiple counties based on statistics, team success, and impact on the field throughout the season. Being named to the All-Area team or earning Player of the Year honors represents a significant achievement for high school athletes and can boost college recruiting prospects.

While the selections focus on Southwest Florida programs, the recognition reflects the strong baseball tradition throughout the broader region including the Treasure Coast. High school baseball in Florida is highly competitive, producing college players and professional prospects each year. The 2026 season saw talented players excel at positions across the diamond, from pitching to hitting to defensive play.

Treasure Coast residents have the chance to vote on the all-time best players from local girls basketball history. The voting recognizes the standout athletes who have competed in Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties over the years.

Voting allows local sports fans to weigh in on which players left the biggest mark on Treasure Coast basketball. The recognition celebrates not just individual achievement but the competitive tradition that continues to develop young athletes across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

Fans who purchased tickets for the postponed game can check with Clover Park for information about rescheduling or exchanges. The Mets continue their homestand with additional games against the Threshers in the coming days, giving local baseball fans other opportunities to attend.

Baseball clubs across Minor League Baseball, including teams in Florida, are celebrating PLAY BALL Weekend with special events and activities. The weekend is designed to promote youth participation in baseball and connect fans with the sport.

The events give local families a chance to enjoy baseball together while introducing children to the game. hero.headline: Lake Worth Beach to host finish of 80-mile ocean paddle June 13 for cystic fibrosis families
hero.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the open Atlantic Ocean this June to raise awareness and funds for families living with cystic fibrosis in the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis. Participants will launch from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13, arriving at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. The endurance trek benefits the Pipers Angels Foundation, which event founder Travis Suit established in honor of his daughter, Piper, diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4.

The crossing is part of a four-day schedule, beginning June 10, with arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove. On Thursday, participants take part in a 4Ocean beach cleanup and a community buffet dinner. Friday brings a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony to honor cystic fibrosis warriors, followed by rest and safety checks before launch night. The fundraiser expects participants from around the world. Paddlers must raise at least $2,000 for the cause, and crew or virtual participants have a $500 minimum. Final contributions are due July 31.

Safety is paramount. All paddlers are required to wear a U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation device, waterproof whistle, and reflective gear during dark hours, Suit said. GPS trackers provided by the event must be worn and active at all times, and mandatory safety meetings will be held. Suit, an avid paddler, was inspired to create the event after learning about the natural respiratory benefits of ocean salt air. The foundation has since grown to provide direct support for cystic fibrosis patients and families, connecting them with resources and community.

Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 to cheer paddlers during a daylong beach celebration marking their arrival. Cystic fibrosis is a life-shortening genetic condition that affects the lungs and digestive system. High-profile community events like this one not only raise funds but also spotlight ongoing needs for research, treatment, and family support. More information, registration, and donation details are available at crossingforcysticfibrosis.com and pipersangels.org.

cards.headline: Beetlejuice musical runs through June 7 at Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
cards.teaser: The Broadway hit brings spooky humor and over-the-top visuals to the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall, with performances through this weekend.
cards.body:
Beetlejuice the musical has landed at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach, running June 2 through June 7. The Broadway hit brings its spooky humor, over-the-top visuals, and heartwarming moments to the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall. Actor Ryan Stajmiger steps into the iconic striped suit to play the mischievous demon beloved from Tim Burton's 1988 film. The musical follows Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teen whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a demon with a flair for trouble.

Stajmiger says one of his favorite parts is laughing with the audience. He gets to break the fourth wall and communicate directly with the audience. Early in the run, he experienced one unexpected moment: he was wearing two wigs, and the second wig came off with the first, leaving him bald for an entire scene. He played with the moment and shared the experience with the audience.

Performances include 7:30 p.m. shows on June 3 and June 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, matinee and evening performances on June 6, and a closing matinee on June 7. Tickets start at $34.50 and are available at kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up, with parental discretion advised.

cards.headline: Complete guide to Fourth of July events on the Treasure Coast for America's 250th birthday
cards.teaser: Celebrations marking the nation's 250th birthday are planned across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties this July.

The Treasure Coast is preparing to celebrate America's 250th birthday this Fourth of July with events planned across the region. Communities in Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties will host festivities to mark this milestone anniversary.

This year's Independence Day carries special significance as the nation reaches its semiquicentennial, or 250th birthday since the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Local governments and community organizations are planning commemorative events to honor the occasion.

Residents can expect traditional Fourth of July activities including fireworks displays, parades, and community gatherings throughout the Treasure Coast. The complete guide provides details on timing, locations, and special programming for the historic celebration.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast walkability rankings reveal most pedestrian-friendly cities
cards.teaser: New EPA data ranks local cities on how easy it is to walk to shops, parks, and services without a car.

New data from the Environmental Protection Agency ranks Treasure Coast cities on walkability, measuring how easily residents can reach shops, parks, and services on foot. Walkability has become an increasingly important factor for residents choosing where to live and for local governments planning future development. Cities with higher walkability scores typically feature sidewalks, crosswalks, mixed-use development that places homes near businesses, and shorter distances between destinations.

The EPA data offers Treasure Coast residents a way to compare their community's pedestrian infrastructure with neighboring cities. These rankings can help inform decisions about housing, transportation planning, and community development priorities across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

cards.headline: Five affordable public golf courses on the Treasure Coast offer options for all skill levels

Five public golf courses on the Treasure Coast offer affordable options for golfers of varying skill levels. The facilities provide accessible tee times and reasonable rates for residents looking to play without joining a private club.

With different difficulty levels available, these courses allow golfers to choose layouts that match their abilities. The combination of good prices and varied challenge makes public golf a popular recreational option for Treasure Coast residents throughout the year.

cards.headline: Florida county's grapefruit featured in $2,000 Jeopardy question

A Florida county's grapefruit was the subject of a $2,000 question on Jeopardy, bringing attention to the state's citrus industry on the nationally televised game show. The high-value clue highlighted the county's reputation for producing quality grapefruit.

Florida's citrus industry has long been a signature part of the state's agriculture and economy, with several counties known for their orange and grapefruit production. Indian River County grapefruit, in particular, has earned recognition for its quality and sweetness, benefiting from the region's climate and soil conditions.

The appearance on Jeopardy represents national recognition for Florida's citrus heritage. While the industry has faced challenges in recent years from disease and development, the game show reference underscores the lasting association between Florida counties and their premium citrus crops.

cards.headline: Best spots to watch Fourth of July fireworks across Palm Beach County

Palm Beach County residents will have multiple options for watching Fourth of July fireworks this year, with communities across the area hosting displays to celebrate Independence Day. The viewing locations offer different vantage points and atmospheres for families and friends gathering to mark the holiday.

Fireworks shows remain a central tradition of Fourth of July celebrations, drawing crowds to beaches, parks, and waterfronts. Planning ahead and knowing the best viewing spots can help residents avoid traffic and secure good positions to see the displays.

With America's 250th birthday adding special significance to this year's celebration, communities are preparing for larger than usual crowds at popular fireworks viewing areas. Residents are encouraged to arrive early to popular locations and follow any local guidelines or restrictions for public gatherings during the holiday.

hero.headline: Jacksonville Mayor Deegan to Address Property Tax Overhaul Headed to November Ballot
hero.body:
Jacksonville Mayor Donna Deegan is expected to discuss the local impact of a major property tax overhaul that state lawmakers passed during a special session Thursday. The measure is now headed to the ballot in November, where Florida voters will decide whether to approve the significant changes to the state's property tax system.

The property tax overhaul emerged from a special legislative session and represents one of the most substantial proposed changes to Florida's tax structure in recent years. State lawmakers advanced the measure through both chambers before sending it to voters for final approval. The plan would affect property owners across Florida, though the specific details of the tax changes and their fiscal impact on local governments remain central to the ongoing discussion.

Mayor Deegan's briefing comes as local officials across Florida work to understand how the proposed overhaul would affect municipal budgets and services. Property taxes serve as a critical revenue source for cities, counties, and school districts throughout the state, funding essential services including public safety, infrastructure, and education. Any significant change to the property tax system could require local governments to adjust their budgets and potentially reconsider service levels or seek alternative revenue sources.

The November ballot will give Florida voters the opportunity to weigh in directly on the tax overhaul. Between now and the election, local officials, advocacy groups, and political organizations are expected to mount campaigns both supporting and opposing the measure. Jacksonville represents one of Florida's largest cities, and the mayor's perspective on the proposal will likely influence discussions in other major metropolitan areas across the state. The outcome of the November vote will determine whether Florida makes sweeping changes to a property tax system that has been in place for decades and affects millions of homeowners and businesses statewide.

cards.headline: Florida Man Arrested for Attempting to Sell Stolen Radioactive Device on Facebook
cards.teaser: Florida Highway Patrol arrested a man who attempted to sell a stolen radioactive device on Facebook, raising serious public safety concerns.
cards.body:
The Florida Highway Patrol took a man into custody after he allegedly tried to sell a stolen radioactive device through Facebook. The arrest highlights the dangers posed when hazardous materials fall into unauthorized hands and are traded through public channels.

Radioactive devices are strictly regulated due to the health and safety risks they pose to the public. These materials are typically used in medical, industrial, or research settings and require special licensing and handling procedures. When such devices are stolen, they create immediate concerns about potential radiation exposure to anyone who comes into contact with them, as well as the possibility that the materials could be misused.

Law enforcement agencies work closely with federal and state regulators to track and recover stolen radioactive materials. The attempt to sell such a device on a popular social media platform demonstrates both the brazenness of some criminals and the challenges authorities face in monitoring illegal trade of dangerous materials through digital marketplaces.

cards.headline: Double Stabbing Near University of South Florida Connected to Tampa Death
cards.teaser: Authorities are investigating a double stabbing near the University of South Florida that is tied to a death in Tampa.
cards.body:
A double stabbing occurred near the University of South Florida campus, and investigators have linked the incident to a death in Tampa. The connection between the two violent events suggests a coordinated criminal investigation is underway.

The proximity to the University of South Florida raises concerns about student and community safety in the area surrounding the campus. Universities typically work closely with local law enforcement to ensure campus security and alert students to potential threats in nearby neighborhoods.

Authorities are working to determine the exact nature of the connection between the stabbing and the Tampa death. Such investigations often involve multiple law enforcement agencies coordinating their efforts to build a comprehensive understanding of the events and identify suspects.

cards.headline: Woman's Body Discovered on Popular South Florida Beach
cards.teaser: The body of a woman washed up on a popular South Florida beach, prompting an investigation by local authorities.
cards.body:
A woman's body was found washed ashore on a popular beach in South Florida. The discovery occurred in an area frequented by residents and tourists, raising questions about the circumstances surrounding her death.

When bodies are discovered on beaches, investigators work to determine whether the death resulted from drowning, foul play, or other causes. Medical examiners conduct autopsies to establish cause of death, while law enforcement checks missing persons reports and works to identify the victim. Coastal currents can carry bodies significant distances, which sometimes complicates investigations.

Beach communities across South Florida attract millions of visitors each year, and local authorities maintain protocols for responding to such discoveries. The investigation will likely involve multiple agencies working to piece together what happened and notify the victim's family.

cards.headline: Florida Man Sues Airboat Company After Alligator Bites His Face
cards.teaser: A Florida man filed a lawsuit against an airboat tour company following an incident in which an alligator bit his face during an excursion.
cards.body:
A man in Florida has filed legal action against an airboat tour company after he was bitten in the face by an alligator. The lawsuit raises questions about safety protocols and liability when wildlife encounters go wrong during commercial tours.

Airboat tours are popular attractions in Florida, particularly in areas like the Everglades where alligators are common. Tour operators are expected to maintain safe distances from wildlife and inform customers about potential dangers. When injuries occur, questions arise about whether the company took adequate precautions and whether customers were properly warned about risks.

Alligator bites can cause serious injuries requiring extensive medical treatment and reconstructive surgery, particularly when they involve the face. The lawsuit will likely center on whether the tour operator exercised reasonable care in protecting passengers from foreseeable wildlife encounters. Florida law governs premises liability and tour operator responsibilities, and courts will examine the specific circumstances of the incident to determine if negligence occurred.

cards.headline: Senator Tuberville Voted in Florida After Tax Records Show Alabama Move
cards.teaser: Senator Tuberville cast a vote in Florida despite tax records indicating he had moved back to Alabama, raising residency questions.
cards.body:
Senator Tuberville voted in Florida after tax records suggest he relocated back to Alabama. The discrepancy between his voting location and apparent tax domicile has sparked questions about where the senator maintains his legal residence.

Voting laws require that individuals cast ballots in the jurisdiction where they maintain legal residence. When public officials maintain homes in multiple states, they must establish one as their primary residence for voting and tax purposes. Tax records serve as one indicator of residency, as they show where individuals claim homestead exemptions and file state income tax returns.

The situation highlights the complex residency requirements that affect both elected officials and ordinary citizens who own property in multiple states. Florida's lack of state income tax makes it an attractive domicile for many Americans, including those who maintain connections to other states. Questions about voting location and legal residence can have political and legal implications, particularly for elected officials whose constituents expect them to maintain clear ties to the states they represent.

cards.headline: College Baseball Foundation Names Florida Gators' King Pitcher of the Year Finalist

hero.headline: One airlifted with traumatic injuries after I-95 SUV-semi wreck in Martin County
hero.body:
A person was airlifted to a trauma center Thursday after a collision between an SUV and a semi-truck on Interstate 95 in Martin County. The crash victim sustained traumatic injuries in the wreck, which required emergency airlift transport for immediate medical care.

The collision involved a sport utility vehicle and a commercial semi-truck on the northbound side of I-95. Emergency responders treated the victim at the scene before arranging the helicopter transport to a regional trauma facility equipped to handle serious injuries.

Traffic on I-95 was affected by the crash response and cleanup operations. First responders worked to clear the scene while investigating the circumstances that led to the collision between the two vehicles.

The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the crash.

First responders arrived at the scene to handle the collision involving multiple vehicles. The crash occurred in a high-traffic area of I-95, one of the main north-south arteries through Martin County that connects communities from Stuart to Hobe Sound.

The full closure of northbound lanes caused significant delays for morning commuters and travelers heading north through the county. Crews worked to investigate the crash, treat any injured parties, and clear the wreckage from the interstate to reopen the roadway.

cards.headline: Community activists rally at Blake Library to save rare Oculina coral reef off Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Dozens gathered at Blake Library in Martin County to oppose the rollback of federal protections for the Oculina Bank, a rare deep-water coral reef found nowhere else on Earth.
cards.body:
Community members packed Blake Library in Martin County after a federally appointed council voted to roll back longstanding protections for the Oculina Bank, a unique deep-water coral reef located off the coast of Fort Pierce. The reef sits hundreds of feet below the surface and thrives in deep, dark waters unlike most coral that requires shallow sunlight. Scientists say the reef is home to more than 2,000 marine species.

Dr. Grant Gilmore, a scientist who previously dove the reef, warned that removing protections could devastate the ecosystem. "Very concerned about an ecosystem point of view, where your fish don't exist in a vacuum, they need a habitat, they need food," Gilmore said. "The coral reef was giving them habitat and food. You take that away, you don't have the fish." Mark Perry, Executive Director of the Florida Oceanographic Society, joined Gilmore in urging the public to help save the reef.

Two proposals would reopen parts of the reef to shrimp trawling, even though scientists say trawling destroyed as much as 90% of the reef before federal protections were implemented decades ago. The proposals followed an executive order issued in April 2025 that directed eight regional councils to find ways to reinvigorate fishing industries. Bob Zales, executive director of the Southeastern Fishing Association, has argued that reopening access is essential for the struggling rock shrimp industry, which has dropped from over 700 trips per year in the mid-1990s to under 100 since 2010.

cards.headline: Martin County beach wins national restoration award
cards.teaser: A beach restoration project in Martin County has received a national award recognizing excellence in coastal preservation efforts.
cards.body:
A Martin County beach has been honored with a national restoration award, recognizing successful efforts to preserve and restore the coastal shoreline. The award acknowledges the work done to protect and rehabilitate the beach environment for both wildlife and public use.

The recognition comes from a national organization that evaluates coastal restoration projects across the country. Martin County's beach project stood out among numerous submissions for its approach to balancing environmental protection with community access to the shore.

The award highlights Martin County's commitment to maintaining its natural coastal resources. Beach restoration projects along the Treasure Coast are critical for protecting shoreline infrastructure, preserving sea turtle nesting habitat, and maintaining recreational beaches for residents and visitors.

cards.body:
An heiress has purchased 8 acres of land in Florida to protect it from development, adding the property to growing conservation efforts across the state. The land acquisition is aimed at preserving natural habitat and preventing commercial or residential construction on the site.

The purchase reflects a broader trend of private conservation efforts in Florida, where development pressure continues to threaten natural areas. By buying and preserving land, private individuals can ensure that ecosystems remain intact and wildlife habitats are protected from bulldozers and construction.

The 8-acre parcel will be maintained in its natural state rather than being converted to housing, shopping centers, or other development. Conservation purchases like this one help preserve Florida's remaining green spaces as the state continues to experience population growth and development pressure.

cards.headline: Florida nuclear power plant to test 91 emergency sirens on June 4
cards.teaser: A Florida nuclear power plant will conduct a test of 91 emergency warning sirens on June 4 as part of its regular safety procedures.
cards.body:
A nuclear power plant in Florida will test 91 emergency sirens on June 4 as part of its routine safety and preparedness procedures. The sirens are designed to alert nearby residents in the event of an emergency at the nuclear facility.

The test will sound sirens throughout the area surrounding the power plant. Residents should expect to hear the warning tones during the scheduled test and should not be alarmed, as this is a planned exercise to ensure the emergency notification system is functioning properly.

Nuclear power plants are required to maintain emergency alert systems and test them regularly to ensure they can quickly notify the public if a serious incident occurs. The siren network provides a critical warning system for communities near the facility, allowing residents time to take protective actions if needed.

cards.headline: Wire 3 to invest $53 million to power up three Martin County communities
cards.teaser: Wire 3 announced a $53 million investment to enhance electrical infrastructure serving three communities in Martin County.
cards.body:
Wire 3 is making a $53 million investment to upgrade power infrastructure in three Martin County communities. The investment will improve electrical service reliability and capacity for residents and businesses in the affected areas.

The infrastructure project will enhance the power grid serving the three communities, which should reduce outages and improve service quality. As Martin County continues to grow, upgrading electrical infrastructure becomes increasingly important to meet demand and prevent service disruptions.

The $53 million commitment represents a significant investment in Martin County's utility infrastructure. Modern, reliable power service is essential for economic development, quality of life, and the ability to handle the county's growing population and business activity.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie woman sentenced to 3 years in prison for running illegal med spa out of backyard shed
hero.body:
Rosa Mena, 50, of Port St. Lucie has been sentenced to three years in prison and five years of probation after operating an illegal medical spa out of a shed in her backyard. Mena ran the business, called Miracle Hand and Spa, out of a makeshift facility at her residence in the 5000 block of Northwest Coosa Drive. A victim came forward to Port St. Lucie Police in May 2025 after experiencing partial facial paralysis following Botox injections performed by Mena. The victim had received 62 units of Botox during a session at the backyard facility after being referred by coworkers who had previously used Mena's services.

When the victim reported the paralysis to Mena, Mena refunded the $325 payment and asked the victim to return for another injection of vitamins to reverse the effects. After the paralysis continued, the victim requested Mena's medical license. Mena provided an altered phlebotomy certificate that investigators later confirmed had expired in February 2024. Mena also told the victim she was a doctor from the Dominican Republic in an attempt to reassure her.

A multi-agency investigation involving Port St. Lucie Police, PSL Code Enforcement, the PSL Building Department, PSL Business Tax, and the Florida Department of Health led to a search warrant at Mena's residence. Detectives found medical beds, fat sculpting machines, laser hair removal equipment, laser liposuction machines, and injection devices for fillers and Botox. The evidence revealed Mena had been operating a full-scale illegal medical facility from the backyard shed.

Mena was charged with three counts of aggravated battery causing bodily harm, three counts of health safety practicing medicine without an active license, one count of fraud to obtain property worth $300 or more, one count of fraud to obtain property under $20,000, and one count of use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony. The case demonstrates the dangers of unlicensed medical procedures and the importance of verifying credentials before receiving cosmetic treatments.

cards.headline: 12 Make-A-Wish kids sworn in as junior deputies at St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office
cards.teaser: Sheriff Richard Del Toro honored 12 young heroes from the Make-A-Wish Foundation by swearing them in as junior deputies on Wednesday.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office hosted a special ceremony on Wednesday where Sheriff Richard Del Toro swore in 12 children from the Make-A-Wish Foundation as junior deputies. Del Toro called it one of the greatest days in his career. The young honorees received badges, toured the sheriff's office, and witnessed demonstrations from the helicopter unit, SWAT team, and K-9 units.

Among the new junior deputies were twins Mia and Daryl Nyack. In 2023, Mia was diagnosed with aplastic anemia, a serious blood disorder, and needed a bone marrow transplant. Her twin brother Daryl donated his bone marrow to save his sister's life, enduring significant pain and spending time in a wheelchair during his recovery. Mia said she was scared but her brother made her feel safe. Another junior deputy, Tobias, was diagnosed with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia in 2022. His mother, Charity Deleon, said Tobias even died at one point but was brought back and miraculously recovered.

The mothers of the junior deputies thanked the sheriff's office for making their children feel special and reminding them they are important members of the community. Sheriff Del Toro turned the gratitude around, telling the children and their families that they made the department's wish come true by leaving an imprint on the deputies and staff who met them.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County considers rocket recovery facility at Port of Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: County officials are evaluating a proposal to establish a rocket recovery facility at the Port of Fort Pierce, potentially bringing space industry operations to the area.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County is considering a proposal to develop a rocket recovery facility at the Port of Fort Pierce. The project would bring space industry infrastructure to the local port, positioning St. Lucie County to participate in the recovery and processing of rocket components from launches along Florida's Space Coast.

The facility would take advantage of the Port of Fort Pierce's waterfront access and proximity to launch sites further north. Rocket recovery operations typically involve retrieving reusable rocket boosters and other components from the ocean after launches. The proposal represents a potential economic development opportunity for St. Lucie County, which has been working to diversify its economic base and attract higher-paying jobs in advanced industries.

County officials are in the evaluation stage of the proposal, reviewing the technical requirements, environmental considerations, and economic benefits of hosting such a facility. The decision could affect the future development direction of the Port of Fort Pierce and the types of marine industrial operations that locate in the area.

cards.headline: Senator Ashley Moody honors Port St. Lucie Sergeant Levasseur with Florida's Finest Award
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie police sergeant received recognition from Senator Ashley Moody with the Florida's Finest Award for outstanding law enforcement service.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Sergeant Levasseur was honored by Senator Ashley Moody with the Florida's Finest Award, recognizing exceptional service in law enforcement. The award highlights the sergeant's contributions to public safety and community policing in Port St. Lucie.

The Florida's Finest Award is presented to law enforcement officers who demonstrate outstanding dedication, professionalism, and service to their communities. Senator Moody, who previously served as Florida's Attorney General before her election to the U.S. Senate, has continued to recognize law enforcement excellence through this award program. The honor reflects both Sergeant Levasseur's individual achievements and the quality of law enforcement service in Port St. Lucie.

The recognition ceremony took place Thursday and was attended by local law enforcement officials and community members. The award adds to Port St. Lucie's reputation for professional police service and community engagement.

cards.headline: Funeral arrangements announced for St. Lucie County firefighter Connor Whitehead
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County community prepares to honor firefighter Connor Whitehead with funeral services following his death.
cards.body:
Funeral arrangements have been announced for St. Lucie County firefighter Connor Whitehead. The announcement provides the community an opportunity to pay respects to Whitehead, who served as a firefighter protecting St. Lucie County residents.

Whitehead's death represents a loss for the St. Lucie County fire service and the broader community that depends on first responders. Firefighters face significant risks in their daily work protecting lives and property, and the loss of a member affects the entire department and the families they serve. The funeral arrangements allow colleagues, friends, and community members to gather and honor Whitehead's service.

The St. Lucie County firefighting community and residents will have the chance to show support for Whitehead's family and fellow firefighters during the services. Details about the funeral provide information for those wishing to attend and pay their respects.

cards.headline: Texas oil mogul's super yacht M5 docks at Fort Pierce marina
cards.teaser: A luxury super yacht owned by a Texas oil industry executive has arrived at a Fort Pierce marina, drawing attention from boating enthusiasts.
cards.body:
The M5, a super yacht owned by a Texas oil mogul, is currently docked at a marina in Fort Pierce. The arrival of the large luxury vessel has attracted interest from local boating enthusiasts and residents who have noticed the impressive craft at the waterfront facility.

Super yachts like the M5 occasionally visit Treasure Coast marinas as their wealthy owners cruise Florida's Atlantic coast. Fort Pierce's deepwater port facilities and marina infrastructure can accommodate large vessels, making it a stopping point for yachts traveling between South Florida and destinations further north. The presence of such vessels highlights Fort Pierce's role as a significant port on Florida's east coast.

The M5's visit is temporary as the yacht continues its travels. Such stops provide economic benefits to local marinas and marine service providers who supply fuel, provisions, and maintenance services to visiting vessels.

cards.headline: Affidavit reveals new details in second St. Lucie County school bus driver molestation case
cards.teaser: Court documents provide additional information about a second molestation case involving a St. Lucie County school bus driver.
cards.body:
An affidavit has been released with new details in a second molestation case involving a St. Lucie County school bus driver. The court document sheds light on the allegations and evidence in the case, which involves a driver who had contact with students while transporting them to and from school.

The case raises serious concerns about student safety on school buses and the vetting and monitoring of drivers who work with children. St. Lucie County school officials and law enforcement have been investigating the allegations. The affidavit provides prosecutors and the public with a clearer picture of what allegedly occurred and the evidence that led to charges.

The revelation of a second case involving a bus driver has heightened awareness among parents in St. Lucie County about transportation safety. School district officials are reviewing their procedures for screening, hiring, and supervising bus drivers to ensure student safety during transportation.

hero.headline: Indian River Mall demolition underway in Vero Beach
hero.body:
Demolition has begun at the Indian River Mall in Vero Beach, marking the end of an era for the longtime shopping center. Crews are now on site tearing down the structure that has served the community for decades.

The demolition has stirred memories among residents who shopped, worked, and gathered at the mall over the years. The Indian River Mall was a central shopping destination in Vero Beach and a familiar landmark in the community.

Local officials have expressed that the project satisfies various stakeholders in the community. The demolition represents a significant change to the commercial landscape of Vero Beach and Indian River County.

The site's redevelopment will reshape a major piece of real estate in the area. Community members have been reflecting on their experiences at the mall as the building comes down, with many sharing photographs and stories from the shopping center's decades of operation.

cards.headline: Ultraluxury apartments open at The Vivien on Indian River Boulevard in Vero Beach
cards.teaser: The Vivien, a new ultraluxury apartment complex on Indian River Boulevard in Vero Beach, is starting to welcome residents.
cards.body:
The Vivien apartment complex on Indian River Boulevard in Vero Beach has begun filling with residents. The ultraluxury development represents a new high-end housing option in the area.

The project adds upscale rental housing to Vero Beach's residential market. Indian River Boulevard, which runs along the waterfront, is a prominent corridor in the city.

The opening of The Vivien reflects continued development and investment in Vero Beach's housing sector. The luxury apartments are attracting residents seeking high-end amenities and a prime location along the boulevard.

cards.headline: WWII veteran Bill Keegan celebrates 102nd birthday in Indian River County
cards.teaser: World War II veteran Bill Keegan marked his 102nd birthday in Indian River County this week.
cards.body:
Bill Keegan, a World War II veteran living in Indian River County, celebrated turning 102 years old. The milestone birthday honors a member of the Greatest Generation who served his country during the war.

Keegan's longevity and military service represent a living connection to one of the most significant periods in American history. Veterans of World War II are increasingly rare, making each birthday celebration particularly meaningful.

The centenarian's birthday was recognized locally as communities across the country work to honor remaining WWII veterans. Indian River County is home to veterans from multiple generations who have contributed to both military service and the local community.

cards.headline: Free Hot Pink concert scheduled Friday at Riverview Park in Sebastian
cards.teaser: A free Hot Pink concert will take place Friday at Riverview Park in Sebastian.
cards.body:
Sebastian residents can enjoy a free concert by the band Hot Pink on Friday at Riverview Park. The event offers live music at no cost to attendees.

Riverview Park serves as a community gathering space in Sebastian and regularly hosts public events. The free concert provides entertainment accessible to all residents regardless of budget.

Friday's performance is the latest in community events that bring residents together for outdoor activities. Sebastian continues to offer recreational and cultural programming through its parks system.

cards.headline: Vero Beach pioneer to receive Florida historical marker
cards.teaser: A Vero Beach pioneer will be honored with a Florida historical marker recognizing their contributions to the community.
cards.body:
A historical marker will be installed in Vero Beach to commemorate a local pioneer who played a significant role in the city's early development. The Florida historical marker program recognizes individuals, events, and places that shaped the state's history.

The marker will serve as a permanent reminder of the pioneer's contributions to Vero Beach and Indian River County. Historical markers help preserve community heritage and educate residents and visitors about local history.

Vero Beach has a rich history dating back to its founding in the early 20th century. The marker joins other historical commemorations throughout Indian River County that document the region's development and the people who built the community.

cards.headline: Florida family of five receives new furnished home with nonprofit help
cards.teaser: A Florida family of five has been given a new furnished home through the efforts of local nonprofit organizations.
cards.body:
Nonprofit organizations have provided a family of five with a new furnished home in Florida. The collaborative effort by charitable groups has given the family stable housing with all necessary furnishings.

The project represents the kind of community support that helps families in need achieve housing security. Multiple nonprofits worked together to make the home ready for the family to move in immediately.

Charitable organizations throughout the Treasure Coast regularly assist families facing housing challenges. This home donation demonstrates how nonprofit collaboration can address critical needs and change lives for local families.

cards.headline: School summer vacation dates set for St. Lucie, Martin and Indian River counties
cards.teaser: Summer vacation dates have been announced for school districts in St. Lucie, Martin and Indian River counties.
cards.body:
School districts in St. Lucie, Martin and Indian River counties have released their summer vacation schedules for students. The dates determine when students finish the current school year and when they return for the new academic year.

Families across the three-county area can now plan summer activities, camps, and vacations around the official school calendar. The summer break provides students with time off from academic instruction while school facilities undergo maintenance and teachers prepare for the upcoming year.

School calendars are set well in advance to allow parents to arrange childcare and make travel plans. The schedules in all three counties guide not only students and teachers but also the many businesses and programs that serve school-age children during summer months.
